articles.title: Sechs Wege zum ewigen Ich: Was Forscher mit Gehirnen anstellen, damit wir nie ganz verschwinden
articles.summary:
Kopf ab, Gehirn rein, Geist hochladen: 6 waghalsige Experimente für ein Leben ohne Körper
Habt ihr schon einmal darüber nachgedacht, was euch zu dem macht, was ihr seid? Die Wissenschaft versichert uns, dass dies ausschließlich mit dem drei Pfund schweren Organ zwischen unseren Ohren zu tun hat – mit seinen Milliarden von Neuronen und Billionen feiner Verbindungen. Viel schwieriger ist es jedoch zu erklären, warum wir ein Selbstbewusstsein haben, oder genau zu bestimmen, wo diese erste Erinnerung an Mama tatsächlich gespeichert ist. Wenn wir älter werden, vergessen wir das meiste, was wir erlebt haben, und doch gibt es eine unbestreitbare Kontinuität: Mit 30, 50 oder 70 wirst du immer noch du selbst sein.
Um diese schwer fassbare Kontinuität des Selbst zu bewahren, arbeiten einige weitsichtige Technologen an Möglichkeiten, dein Gehirn am Laufen zu halten – sogar über den Tod hinaus. Nennen wir sie die „Mind Saver“. Sie erforschen alles, vom Einfrieren von Gehirnen in flüssigem Stickstoff über die Verbesserung lebender Gehirne bis hin zum Hochladen unserer Erinnerungen in die Cloud. Hier betrachten wir sechs mögliche und teilweise auch verrückte Wege, um euren Geist am Leben zu erhalten. Wir ordnen ein, wie realisierbar sie wären und welche Vorteile die heutige Forschung mit sich bringen könnte – selbst wenn die kognitive Unsterblichkeit nicht gelingen sollte.

articles.title: When Electric Cars Were the Clean, Quiet Choice for Women
articles.summary:
At the turn of the last century, the automobile industry was still new and evolving rapidly. In 1898, there were about 50 carmakers in the United States. A decade later, that number had increased fivefold. In 1901, the companies produced 7,000 vehicles. By 1910, production had reached 181,000.
For several decades, electric cars vied with those powered by steam and internal combustion, and nobody was sure which technology would come out on top. Steam had the legacy of locomotive technology behind it but came with a risk of fire. Steam-powered vehicles could also become exceedingly hot, depending on the placement of the boiler and the steam piping. Both gasoline and electric cars faced logistical challenges: How far could you travel without refueling or charging? You could always throw an extra can of gasoline in the back of the car, but charging a battery involved more planning. The infrastructure for long-distance travel was not yet in place.
Before the invention of the electric starter in 1911, gasoline-powered engines had to be started with a hand crank; once running, they were loud and emitted noxious fumes. Fully electric vehicles, by contrast, were easy to start; you just turned on the main battery switch, often with a key, and there was no foul exhaust to deal with.

articles.title: Syrian Hacker Gets Prison Time in US After Over a Decade on the Run
articles.summary:
A Syrian man tied to the Syrian Electronic Army (SEA) has received a 42-month prison sentence in the US, more than 12 years after he was first charged.
Ahmad Umar Agha, who used the online handle Th3Pr0, was sentenced on Thursday by a federal court in the Eastern District of Virginia. According to the Justice Department, he evaded US authorities for more than a decade.
Prosecutors say the hacking conspiracy Agha took part in was directed by figures close to Bashar al-Assad, among them the head of Syria’s General Intelligence Directorate. The scheme began as early as August 2011 and continued until January 2024.
The DOJ described Agha as a central figure in the operation. He compromised around 47 targets, a mix of Western news outlets, companies, NGOs, and government bodies in the US and allied countries.
Among the intrusions highlighted by prosecutors was the 2013 takeover of the Associated Press’s Twitter account. Agha used it to publish a fabricated report claiming that President Barack Obama had been hurt in two blasts at the White House. The fake post triggered a flash crash that briefly wiped $136 billion off the combined value of the Dow Jones Industrial Average’s component stocks.
Agha also gained access to the company hosting the Marine Corps’ recruiting website and sent its traffic to an image calling on Marines to defy their orders.

Google-Cloud für BND und Verfassungsschutz: Warum dieser Geheimdienst-Deal ein Hohn für die digitale Souveränität ist
Die Messe schien gelesen. Nach ausgiebiger Diskussion über das Thema digitale Souveränität, um das sich lange nur auf dem Papier bemüht wurde, kam in jüngster Vergangenheit auch in der Politik endlich deutlich mehr Bewegung in das Thema. Das zwang sogar Microsoft, das mit Microsoft 365 eine der meistgenutzten Enterprise-Kollaborationslösungen vertreibt, dazu, sein Angebot nochmal für den europäischen Markt nachzudrehen. Ein Stück weit hatte man die US-Tech-Firmen da, wo man sie haben wollte.
Dass diese Bewegung gerade von einer Seite torpediert wird, die sich ein bisschen mehr mit Themen wie Datenschutz und Hintertüren auskennen sollte, ist fast schon bizarr. articles.title: From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era.
articles.summary:
Finding a real security flaw and getting paid for it is an appealing goal when you are learning cyber security. Bug bounties give you a chance to test your skills on real software and help its developers make it safer.
Headlines about programs closing or pausing under a flood of AI reports can make that route feel less certain.
Earlier this year, curl, the widely used data transfer tool and library, ended its paid bounty program after similar problems.
As a beginner, these decisions raise a practical question about where to put your effort.
A useful starting point is understanding what went wrong, then building the skills to produce findings that someone else can verify.
Why some bug bounty programs are pulling back
A bug bounty program rewards eligible security findings under a defined set of rules. Developers must still review each submission, reproduce the issue and assess its impact.
A convincing report about an imaginary vulnerability can consume time that a small security team needs for genuine problems.
When curl ended its program on January 31, 2026, maintainer Daniel Stenberg explained how the quality of submissions had deteriorated. He confirmed vulnerabilities fell from above 15% in previous years to below 5% starting in 2025. Across its lifetime, the program had helped uncover 87 confirmed vulnerabilities and paid researchers more than $100,000.
Those figures describe curl’s experience specifically.

En España, el Gobierno ha intentado abordar este desafío vinculando la expansión de los centros de datos a la generación renovable, de manera que no supongan un peaje altísimo que obligue al sistema eléctrico a recurrir a más generación fósil o a incrementar la presión sobre los precios.
Sin embargo, y aunque se ha presentado recientemente un nuevo borrador mucho más suave, este nuevo texto sigue insistiendo en la misma idea de fondo sobre la exigencia de renovables. Los centros de datos trabajan todo el día, las renovables no. Tanto el borrador que se presentó en agosto como la revisión que se ha hecho estos días contemplan que los centros de datos tendrán que ir acompañados de nueva generación renovable. Se mantiene el objetivo de cubrir, como mínimo, el 80% del suministro eléctrico con energía solar o eólica (adicionalidad renovable), y que el 80% del consumo esté respaldado hora a hora (correlación horaria). articles.title: Reddit to lock content behind logins to fight scrapers
articles.summary:
Reddit announced in a post by co-founder Steve Huffman that the site will gradually become a "logged-in service," offering limited access to visitors without accounts.
For the past 20 years, the discussion platform has let users browse almost all its content without logging in, but according to Huffman, Reddit has now grown to a size where this is no longer sustainable.
The two main points for this upcoming change are the need to offer users more personalization and to address the increasing problem of content scrapers.
To tackle this, a new pilot test will begin in selected markets outside the United States in the coming months, requiring users to log in to access the site's full content.
However, what content will be restricted, what countries will be impacted first, and rollout timelines have not been determined at this time.
Huffman said they currently believe it’s important to keep the front page accessible to all, and allow people arriving from search results or other external sources to see at least the page the URL points to.
With users logged in, Reddit expects to gather more data from upvotes to help users find relevant content, join communities, and participate in discussions.
"Our goal is to help you find what’s most relevant to you and drive the community, connection and belonging that makes Reddit, reddit,” explained Huffman.

articles.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
articles.summary:
A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a recently patched Android vulnerability, dubbed "SMS of Death" and tracked as CVE-2026-58882, that lets attackers remotely disrupt cellular service or crash phones by sending a specially crafted text message.
The zero-click denial-of-service flaw can interrupt ongoing calls, including emergency calls, without requiring any interaction from the target. What's worse, Android processes the message before it reaches the SMS inbox, leaving victims with no visible indication of what caused their phones to crash.
According to the vulnerability researcher, Mark Blah, Google reportedly patched the vulnerability in its October 2026 Android security updates for Android 14 through 17. However, the flaw is not listed in Google's October security bulletin, and older Android 12 and 13 devices remain vulnerable because they did not receive the fix.
Blah published a technical analysis of the flaw, caused by improper validation of a header-length value in Android's WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu function.
To exploit the flaw, an attacker can send the following malformed eight-byte WAP Push message to targeted phones:
01 06 88 80 80 80 00 BE   → sent as a data SMS to port 2948
When this value is translated into a signed 32-bit integer without a bounds check, it becomes -2147483648.
When Android attempts to allocate memory using this negative value, it triggers a NegativeArraySizeException that crashes the com.android.phone process.…

Aquella mole sobrevivió a Stalin, a la Segunda Guerra Mundial y a la desaparición del país que la había construido. Más de un siglo después, su futuro está en manos de las autoridades rusas, que consideran demasiado costoso restaurarla y plantean desmontarla para levantar una versión nueva. Sí, Rusia está dispuesta a conservar la idea de uno de sus mayores prodigios de ingeniería, incluso si para hacerlo tiene que destruirla.
La Torre Eiffel soviética. La Torre Shújov, situada al sur del centro de Moscú, fue encargada por Lenin y terminada en 1922. Diseñada por el ingeniero Vladímir Shújov, alcanza los 148 metros y está formada por una sucesión de estructuras hiperbólicas de acero entrelazado.
Su función era transmitir señales de radio por el territorio soviético y simbolizar las ambiciones tecnológicas del nuevo Estado comunista. La ligereza de su diseño la convirtió en una referencia de la arquitectura moderna y en una respuesta simbólica a la Torre Eiffel, inaugurada en París en 1889.
Un siglo resistiendo. La estructura atravesó las purgas estalinistas, la invasión alemana de la Unión Soviética y el colapso del régimen en 1991. Su deterioro llegó de una forma mucho menos espectacular, con décadas de mantenimiento insuficiente. La última vez que se pintó fue en 1964 y dejó de utilizarse en gran medida para las transmisiones a finales de 2001.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges nearly 30%, its worst day in 52 years

What just happened? Intel was one of the stock market's biggest surprises this year. Its shares nearly quadrupled between January and a record high in late June – a run fueled by demand for the CPUs behind agentic AI. But on Friday, the chipmaker gave back a huge chunk of those gains in a single session. The stock closed down almost 29% at $65.76, its worst day since 1974.
Oddly enough, the quarter itself went well. Intel beat Wall Street's earnings estimates. Its data center revenue jumped nearly 80% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, too. But its forecast for the last three months of the year landed well short: analysts had penciled in about $17 billion in revenue. Intel only expects $15 billion to $16 billion.
The weak spot is PCs. AI data centers are buying up so much of the world's memory that laptops and desktops have gotten a lot pricier this year. So fewer of them are selling. Intel now expects PC shipments to drop about 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. It doesn't see things improving until memory supply and prices get back to normal.
The forecast also has to absorb a shutdown at the company's fab in Kiryat Gat, Israel. That's where an explosion killed two workers earlier this month.

Die Nutzung ist freiwillig. Wer kein Smartphone hat oder das digitale Angebot einfach nicht nutzen will, kann also weiter auf die physischen Ausweisdokumente zurückgreifen. Nutzen lässt sich d-you ab 16 Jahren und nur auf einem Smartphone mit NFC und Android oder iOS, alternative Betriebssysteme werden nicht unterstützt. Außerdem braucht die Ausweisfunktion eine Internetverbindung. Geht das Handy verloren, muss die Wallet ohne Backup komplett neu eingerichtet werden.
Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Ab Ende 2027 sind dann auch Banken, Energieversorger, Telekommunikationsanbieter und sehr große Online-Plattformen verpflichtet, die Wallet zu nutzen. In an interview on the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman argued that it's more efficient to direct the world's tightening supply of memory to AI data centers than to local devices. The comments drew immediate backlash as hardware prices continue to climb.

Google PageBreak uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities, but reports them only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application, resulting in a near-zero false-positive rate.
With PageBreak, every vulnerability hypothesis is tested against a running environment with a real exploit, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing to a world-readable location for path traversal, or triggering outbound DNS for RCE. Michał Bentkowski, information security engineer at Google, explains:
Early on in the development of PageBreak, we made a conscious decision to prioritize deterministic validation. Rather than simply hypothesizing bugs based on code patterns, the system closes the loop by verifying potential flaws against running environments. This approach results in a near-zero false positive rate, ensuring that we avoid overloading product teams with unverified vulnerability reports.
Google also retains non-deterministic findings internally to seed deeper future scans, identify gaps in its validation capabilities, and guide the development of new validators. articles.title: Microsoft's DirectX update could slash ray tracing memory by up to 90 percent
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Plenty of ray-traced games still bounce light off cheaper, low-detail copies of their scenery rather than the models players actually see on screen. That's mostly because rebuilding the GPU's ray tracing data for every swaying tree and moving character each frame simply takes too long. A new DirectX feature currently in preview aims to fix that. It could also free up a big chunk of the video memory ray tracing currently eats.
Microsoft detailed Clustered Geometry and a companion feature called Partitioned TLAS on its DirectX developer blog this week, describing the pair as the biggest change to DirectX Raytracing since the API arrived in 2018.
Right now, any time a mesh deforms or streams in at a new level of detail, the GPU has to rebuild that object's acceleration structure from scratch. Clustered Geometry instead splits models into small chunks of up to 256 triangles that get built once and reused. So when an object changes, developers can reassemble existing clusters or rebuild just a handful of them.
Partitioned TLAS applies similar thinking to the whole scene. It breaks the world into regions so that only the parts where something actually moved get updated each frame.
Microsoft's own test sample makes the gains look enormous. On a Radeon RX 9070, switching from conventional rebuilds to clustered geometry lifted the frame rate from 1.2 fps to 79 fps. Per-frame build time dropped from 788ms to just over 3ms, and memory for those structures shrank fro…

A study published on October 22 in the journal Forensic Science International reports that researchers from Curtin University in Perth, Australia, have developed a forensic method to analyze 3D-printed PLA parts and match them to their respective filament, correctly matching 26 out of 28 samples of PLA. articles.title: Shielding the patch gap: The exploit doesn't wait for Patch Tuesday
articles.summary:
Shielding the patch gap: The exploit doesn’t wait for Patch Tuesday
Four years after Log4Shell became one of the most consequential vulnerabilities in software history, vulnerable instances of the library are still turning up in production environments. That persistence isn’t really a failure of tooling. It’s a fact of how modern applications are built. A typical service pulls in hundreds of transitive open-source dependencies, any one of which can carry a critical CVE that’s difficult to even inventory, let alone test and ship a fix for on short notice.
Now factor in what AI-assisted vulnerability research is starting to do to that timeline. Attackers can already use large language models to trace exploit paths through unfamiliar codebases and generate working proof-of-concept variants in hours rather than weeks. If that trend holds, security teams are no longer planning for one Log4Shell-scale event every few years. They are preparing for dozens running concurrently, each with a shrinking window between disclosure and exploitation.
Patching is necessary. It just isn’t sufficient on its own.
Patching remains the durable fix, but compensating controls can augment that longer cycle. The interval between “we know we’re vulnerable” and “we’ve safely shipped the fix” is set by dependency scanning, regression testing, change-management windows, and who owns the affected service, not by how fast an advisory gets published. That interval between the patch release date and the date i…

Fortanix has announced support for Confidential Containers in its Confidential AI platform. The integration connects Kubernetes workload attestation to encryption-key release, so workloads that meet security policy can decrypt models and sensitive data inside hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs).
Confidential Containers (CoCo), a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, runs Kubernetes pods inside confidential virtual machines backed by hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs). Unlike ordinary containers, whose isolation depends largely on the host operating system, confidential VMs use hardware protections to encrypt memory and restrict access to the workload while it runs. This helps protect data in use, not just data at rest or in transit, and can let teams run sensitive workloads on shared infrastructure. Those protections still depend on trusting the guest software and configuring attestation and key release correctly.
Fortanix's technical overview describes plugins connecting CoCo workloads to two services: Confidential Computing Manager (CCM), which verifies the environment, and Data Security Manager (DSM), which releases keys only to environments CCM has verified. Und das ist primär seine Interaktivität. In einem Game läuft, anders als in einem Film, im besten Fall nichts von allein ab. Erst wenn eine Taste gedrückt oder ein Stick nach vorn geschoben wird, geht es weiter. Das aber kann einiges an Überwindung kosten.
Der Horror der Einschränkung
Kaum jemand kann wohl besser über die psychologischen Prozesse des Horrorspiels sprechen, als Psycholog:innen. Besonders jene, die selbst gerne spielen. Wie das Videospiel die Erwartungen und Handlungsfähigkeit der Spieler:innen kontrollieren und manipulieren kann, erklärt der Psychologe André Markus anhand von P.T. In dem Game laufen die Spieler:innen immer wieder durch den gleichen Flur, in dem unvorhersehbare Dinge passieren – und der Geist einer Frau sein Unwesen treibt.

articles.title: Intra-African payment rails are key to cutting cross-border friction, says Grey - TechCabal

Grey is building its own payment connections between African markets to make cross-border transfers more reliable and to secure the foreign currency needed to settle them, Idorenyin Obong, its co-founder and chief executive, said at a press briefing at Moonshot by TechCabal 2026 on Thursday.
“We have invested in building rails within Africa,” Obong said.
Grey lets individuals and businesses send and receive money across markets including Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana. Moving money between African countries remains slow and costly because payment systems are fragmented, each conversion adds a fee, and dollars or other foreign currency are often scarce.
Obong named two problems. The first is reliability: making sure money arrives when the customer was told it would. The second is liquidity: finding enough of the right currency to complete the transfer. Grey has partnered with providers across its markets to source those currencies and settle transfers in real time, he said.
Most transfers between two African currencies have traditionally gone through the US dollar first. Grey says it now converts directly between some African currencies.
“The crux of the matter is that there used to be a need for an intermediary, but we have built out these exotic currency pairs so that you don’t have to go that extent,” Obong said.

articles.title: OpenBSD 8.0 Brings Expanded Hardware Support, Security Enhancements, and Virtualization Improvements
articles.summary:
OpenBSD 8.0 is a substantial upgrade bringing broader hardware compatibility, enhanced security, an expanded virtual address space, and support for modern architectures, including Intel Arc A-Series graphics support, ARM64 hibernation, RISC-V improvements, and enhanced virtual machine support.
Key hardware and virtualization improvements in OpenBSD 8.0 include a larger virtual address space for the AMD64 kernel, expanded from 4 GB to 512 GB, enabling it to map graphics cards with more than 4 GB of VRAM; support for multi-processor virtual machines through vmm/vmd, with up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest and improvements to virtual hardware and guest compatibility; expanded RISC-V support, including the 'V' vector extension and Advanced Interrupt Architecture, improving compatibility with newer processors and platforms; and arm64 hibernation support, alongside faster swap encryption using AES instructions.
Although OpenBSD 8.0 introduces support for the Intel Arc A-Series GPUs, based on the DG2/Alchemist architecture, NVIDIA GPUs remain unsupported, partially due to the fact that NVIDIA does not provide proprietary binary drivers for OpenBSD, unlike Linux and FreeBSD.
OpenBSD 8.0 also expands peripheral support, including the riscv64 K3 PCIe/USB3 combo PHY, the SpacemiT K3 SoC and PCIe controller, as well as the Intel E610 and Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake Ethernet devices. articles.title: Verve plans phone tap-to-pay and AI agent payments
articles.summary:
Verve, Nigeria’s largest card scheme, plans to let customers pay by tapping their phones and, eventually, to let AI assistants make payments on their behalf, its chief executive, Vincent Ogbunude, said on Thursday.
Speaking on the Big Tech and Enterprise Stage at Moonshot by TechCabal on 29 October, Ogbunude described the plans as the next step in removing friction from payments. “The greatest cost in payments is friction,” he said. Every extra step, from typing an account number to retrying a failed transfer, adds cost, he argued.
The plans build on a push Verve began last year. TechCabal reported in December that Verve had passed 100 million cards and was moving into contactless payments and tokenisation, which replaces card details with a one-time code. Verve now has 130 million cards, Ogbunude said.
Tap-to-pay on phones would let customers pay with a device they already carry, without a physical card. Agentic payments go further: an AI assistant, acting on a customer’s instructions, would find and complete a purchase without the customer handling each step.
Global card networks are moving the same way. Visa and Mastercard both announced programmes in 2025 to let AI agents make payments for cardholders.
Verve is the card scheme of Interswitch, the Nigerian payments company. Ogbunude framed Interswitch’s history as a run of fixes for friction: before it, customers had to visit their own bank’s branch to withdraw cash; its network let them use cards at any bank’s ATM, and it…

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. articles.title: Veteran Microsoft engineer makes his own RAM from scratch using AI — custom FPGA board dodges extreme 1970s PDP-11 memory prices
articles.summary:
Veteran Microsoft engineer makes his own RAM from scratch using AI — custom FPGA board dodges extreme 1970s PDP-11 memory prices
The times are hard for us all.
Dave Plummer, former Microsoft engineer and wizard of Task Manager, Windows Pinball, and now TMOG, has an interesting project in his hands once again. After seeing exactly how many zeros were in the price tag for a megabyte of memory for his vintage PDP-11, he decided to take matters into his own hands and conjure up a new RAM board.
The PDP-11 is from 1970, and later models could fit in as much as four megabytes of memory. Plummer enlisted the help of ChatGPT and the EasyEDA online circuit simulator, though he notes that he hadn't done complicated projects like this before. As several PDP-11 models used Q-Bus boards for main system components, he designed this RAM as a standalone card, then tested it on a backplane alongside another board containing the system's M8190 CPU.
Atop it, he placed a Lattice MachXO2 FPGA serving as a memory controller (model 2000HC, if you're wondering), connected to four ISSI 1 MB memory chips. After adding a U2S I/O chip, a bank of DIP switches, comm ports, and sprinkling a handful of capacitors, he had a complete circuit. The M8190 board design has a 22-bit bus and reserves the top 256 KB for I/O and ROM.
However, it wasn't a first-time-lucky project. Plummer encountered a few abortive starts, as he'd never flash-programmed an FPGA chip before. He fixed that after a few attempts, but then…

Five years after the fork, OpenSearch is slowly stepping out of AWS’s shadow
OpenSearch has come a long way since Amazon Web Services first announced the project back in January 2021, in response to Elastic’s decision to move Elasticsearch and its accompanying visualization tool, Kibana, away from Apache 2.0 and onto a combination of proprietary and source-available licenses. Elastic said at the time that the reason was to prevent cloud behemoths such as AWS from offering Elasticsearch “as a service” without giving anything back, while also accusing AWS of violating the Elasticsearch trademark.
While Elastic subsequently returned Elasticsearch and Kibana to open source by adding AGPL as a licensing option, making up with AWS along the way, OpenSearch has continued forging its own path as an independent open source project — albeit one still closely associated with the technology giant that created it.
Reducing the AWS dependency
A major milestone came in September 2024, when AWS transferred OpenSearch to the Linux Foundation, establishing the OpenSearch Software Foundation and placing the project under “vendor-neutral” governance. The move was intended to give other companies greater confidence that they could contribute to OpenSearch without AWS retaining ultimate control over its future.
Two years on, OpenSearch shows signs of gaining traction beyond its original backer. Figures provided to The New Stack by the OpenSearch Software Foundation show that AWS’s share of contrib…

articles.title: Cloudflare’s Post-Quantum GeoKey Manager Enters Closed Beta Without Attribute-Based Encryption
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has moved a post-quantum rebuild of GeoKey Manager into closed beta, protecting geographically fenced decryption keys with a hybrid of ML-KEM-768 and X25519 and replacing the attribute-based encryption the service has relied on since 2022. The beta opened on October 23 to existing Data Localization Suite customers, with general availability planned for the first quarter of 2027.
Chetan Agrawal, Arka Nayan and Erik Engstrom describe the redesign as addressing two requirements at once: data sovereignty rules that confine plaintext processing to a region, and harvest-now, decrypt-later attacks in which traffic captured today is decrypted once a quantum computer exists. GeoKey Manager first shipped in 2017 for TLS keys and moved to ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption in 2022. Cloudflare gives two reasons for dropping that scheme: no production-ready post-quantum variant exists, and customers don't need the large number of regions it was built to express.
In its place, key protection uses HPKE, the hybrid public-key encryption construction defined in RFC 9180, with a key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) combining ML-KEM-768 and X25519, HKDF-SHA-256 and AES-256-GCM. Two kinds of keys replace the policy expressions. Regional root keys are 256-bit symmetric secrets held one per region. articles.title: La physique quantique en ébullition : la théorie du « surfeur quantique » est de nouveau bousculée

Il y a presque cent ans, au cinquième congrès Solvay à Bruxelles, naissait la mécanique quantique moderne. Deux visions du monde s’y affrontaient.
D’un côté, l’école de Copenhague, menée par le Danois Niels Bohr, l’inventeur du premier modèle d’atome à orbites quantifiées, et par les Allemands Werner Heisenberg et Max Born, les architectes de son formalisme mathématique. Pour eux, le monde est intrinsèquement aléatoire, gouverné par le hasard et les probabilités et ne peut être compris avec nos concepts habituels d’espace, de temps et de causalité.
De l’autre côté, Albert Einstein défendait le « déterminisme » classique de Newton et de Laplace, selon lequel chaque objet suit une trajectoire précise dans l’espace et le temps, seulement déterminée par ses conditions initiales. Ce duel, résumé par la boutade d’Einstein « Dieu ne joue pas aux dés », est devenu légendaire.
On oublie qu’une troisième voie fut proposée lors de ce même congrès par l’aristocrate et physicien français Louis de Broglie. Longtemps dénigrée, reniée par de Broglie lui-même, cette explication résiste pourtant toujours aujourd’hui à l’épreuve de l’expérience.

Dès 1923, Louis de Broglie avait eu l’intuition révolutionnaire d’associer une onde à chaque électron, imposant ainsi une nature duale (c’est-à-dire à la fois onde et particule) à la matière pour expliquer les orbites atomiques quantifiées de Bohr. The context problem: How Docusign built agents that understand the business behind contracts
Ask a general-purpose language model to summarize a contract, and it will probably do a reasonable job. Ask it to calculate what a company owes a supplier, accounting for three amendments, a revised pricing schedule, and an internal procurement policy, and it’s a different story.
Enterprise AI agents need to know more than what’s written in a document. They need context about which contracts belong together, which terms still apply, and when a decision needs human approval.
It’s a problem Docusign is tackling as it expands beyond electronic signatures into an Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) platform.. Introduced in April 2024 and available in the U.S. to customers that May, the IAM platform helps organizations create, commit to and manage agreements.
At the center of that effort is Docusign Iris, the contract AI engine that powers Docusign IAM and its AI features across the agreement lifecycle. It combines Docusign’s contract management expertise, agreement-centric data, and AI models to help teams surface insights and take action across contract workflows.
“General LLMs are great. It’s just that you need more around it to really unleash its full power,” Sagnik Nandy, Docusign’s chief technology officer, tells The New Stack.

Am 24. Oktober 2001 erreichte die Raumsonde 2001 Mars Odyssey der US-Weltraumbehörde Nasa ihre Umlaufbahn um den Nachbarplaneten und hält sich dort seit nunmehr 25 Jahren im Dienst. Gemeinsam mit dem seit 2006 aktiven Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), der vom Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) im kalifornischen Pasadena betreut wird, bildet die Sonde das Rückgrat für die Erforschung und den Funkverkehr am Mars.
Mars Odyssey und MRO: Warum die Nasa-Sonden als Funkrelais gebraucht werden
Seit dem Eintritt in die Umlaufbahn hat Mars Odyssey den Planeten mehr als 100.000 Mal umrundet und mit ihrer Infrarotkamera über eine Million Aufnahmen erstellt, wie der Hersteller Lockheed Martin auflistet. Weil die Sendeleistung der Rover auf der Marsoberfläche nicht ausreicht, um große Datenmengen direkt über die rund 225 Millionen Kilometer zur Erde zu schicken, leiten Odyssey und MRO diese Signale als sogenannte Relaisstationen im Ultrakurzwellenbereich weiter.
Gesteuert wird Mars Odyssey dabei von einem gegen Weltraumstrahlung abgeschirmten Prozessor des Typs RAD6000, dessen Architektur noch aus den Neunzigerjahren stammt und mit maximal 20 Megahertz taktet. Wie Wired berichtet, bezeichnet die Planetenforscherin Briony Horgan von der Purdue University im US-Bundesstaat Indiana die zwei Sonden als „entscheidend“ für das gesamte Mars-Programm der Behörde.

articles.title: Hay una "ciudad" que se quedó en España por una palabra y hoy es un trozo de territorio español rodeado por Francia
articles.summary:
En España hay unas cuantas anomalías fronterizas, como la de Ventorros de Balerma o la eterna pugna entre Teruel y Cuenca por un buen puñado de hectáreas. Pero, de todas ellas, la más alucinante es la que aísla a una villa española en Francia. Parece diseñada para poner a prueba los nervios de un cartógrafo. Llívia es un municipio español en plena Cerdaña francesa, rodeado por completo por Francia y conectado con el resto de España por una carretera que atraviesa suelo francés. No es ningún error del mapa, sino la pura consecuencia de una negociación diplomática del siglo XVII.
La historia suele resumirse así: cuando España tuvo que entregar 33 pueblos de la Cerdaña a Francia, sus negociadores defendieron que Llívia no era un pueblo, sino una villa. Pero lo que aquí interesa es su historia, porque va mucho más allá de una mera negociación.
Una guerra de 24 años. Para entenderlo hay que volver a 1659. España y Francia llevaban desde 1635 enfrentadas en una guerra por la hegemonía europea, que terminó con el Tratado de los Pirineos, firmado en la Isla de los Faisanes, en el Bidasoa. España cedió a Francia el Rosellón y el Conflent, entre otros territorios, pero el trazado en la Cerdaña quedó pendiente porque fronteras históricas, jurisdicciones locales y geografía no encajaban. El tratado encargó a comisarios de ambas coronas decidir qué localidades pasaban a Francia.

articles.title: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
OpenAI’s latest funding round isn’t quite living up to expectations, according to multiple news reports.
OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation, ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that.
The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target.
A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment. The company’s reported funding challenges could be blamed, in part, on bad timing, as Wall Street investors have become wary of heavy AI infrastructure spending, leading to a major sell off of tech stocks. And Anthropic’s planned IPO could be facing challenges, too.

articles.title: Ya podemos medir el hidrógeno cósmico sin mapas de galaxias. Es un paso clave para entender la energía oscura

Por eso se usa la metáfora del globo. Si las visualizamos como puntos dibujados en un globo, cuando este se va inflando se separan cada vez más. Hoy en día sabemos que, además, esa expansión se está acelerando con el tiempo. Se cree que esto se debe a una energía misteriosa, bautizada como energía oscura. Ahora, un equipo internacional de científicos ha dado un paso para poder comprobarlo, midiendo la emisión de hidrógeno neutro procedente del Universo. Para ello han usado un método que ya existía, pero lo han perfeccionado.
CHIME. El Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) es un experimento que mide el hidrógeno procedente de distintas ubicaciones del Universo. Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand — company navigating 'one of the most significant supply shortages in history'
Client platforms struggle to get memory anyway, right?
Although the consumer PC market is shrinking and will continue to shrink in the coming quarters, Intel is confident that the overwhelming demand from the AI industry for everything that can compute or store data will offset declines in the client space. To that end, the company is reallocating some of its capacity from client to data center CPUs, expanding its Fab 24 in Ireland to make more Xeons, has begun equipment installation into Fab 62 in Arizona ahead of schedule and vows to make 18A chips there, and is expanding its advanced packaging capacity in New Mexico and Malaysia.
"The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in history, driven by the unprecedented demand for Super Intelligence," said Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, during the company's earnings call. "Against this backdrop, I am pleased by the progress we made growing our server supply in Q3. I am mindful about the ongoing challenges we face in the future quarters to keep pace with server demand."
More Intel 3-based Xeons

articles.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis.
Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act.
xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue.
“Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision.
Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.”

articles.title: Extraterrestres, disparos, ciencia ficción y filosofía. Esto es lo que debes saber de 'Hope', la película que causa sensación y se estrena en España
articles.summary:
Hope (2026), escrita y dirigida por el cineasta coreano Na Hong-jin, podría parecer otra película de ciencia ficción sobre el primer encuentro extraterrestre. O quizás, solo un relato escalofriante sobre una amenaza terrorífica que debe ser combatida por un grupo de esforzados protagonistas. Y de hecho, es ambas cosas. Pero también es una brillante premisa de acción y una radical historia sobre el amor y la búsqueda de propósito. Todo con un apartado visual que sorprende y, además, un giro final que dejará boquiabiertos a los fanáticos.
Pero la producción más costosa en toda la historia del cine de Corea del Sur (tiene un presupuesto de 74 millones de dólares) asombra por ser imprevisible. En especial, porque esta mezcla de ciencia ficción, acción y horror corporal ha redefinido el cine de monstruos contemporáneo. En específico, porque la cinta sumerge al espectador en una experiencia puramente visceral de casi tres horas de metraje. Un largo recorrido en que el suspenso constante, el caos ininterrumpido y un humor negro sumamente particular se entrelazan. Todo para desafiar los límites narrativos de los diferentes géneros. A la vez, subvertir la idea de cómo debe contarse una visión sobre el tiempo, el espacio y la vida fuera de nuestro planeta.
Para eso, la trama se traslada a Hope Harbor. Esta, una pequeña y pacífica localidad fronteriza ubicada en las cercanías de la Zona Desmilitarizada (DMZ) entre ambas Coreas. La tensa cotidianidad de la comunidad se quiebra por comple…

articles.title: Echte Polwanderung: Warum der Nordpol jährlich 10 cm wandert
articles.summary:
Echte Polwanderung: Warum der Nordpol nicht fest an seinem Platz bleibt
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.

articles.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
articles.summary:
The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century.
NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope’s orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.
The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies’ current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope’s performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.
“The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032,” NASA wrote in the RFI. The contractor would be responsible for providing the launch vehicle, servicing spacecraft, mission operations, and “crew if applicable.”

articles.title: La crisis del alquiler obliga cada vez a más jóvenes españoles a vivir sin salón: "Me di cuenta de que sí lo necesito"
articles.summary:
Dormitorios, cocina, baño, pasillos y salón. Con suerte, quizás también una terracita en la que disfrutar del sol. Cuando uno piensa en un apartamento lo primero que se le viene a la cabeza es ese esquema, básico, elemental, común tanto a los pisos de las zonas residenciales más caras como a los de la periferia. Sin embargo, para cada vez más jóvenes que viven de alquiler la realidad es otra: en busca de mayores rentabilidades, sus caseros están eliminando las zonas comunes para aumentar el número de inquilinos.
Es un nuevo síntoma de ‘la España hacinada’.
Adiós, salón. Hilal tiene 21 años, es austriaca, estudia informática automotriz y vive de alquiler en Málaga en un piso de universitarios. Hasta ahí nada del otro mundo. Lo curioso es que en realidad Hilal no duerme en una habitación, sino en un salón reconvertido en cuarto, con su cama, escritorio, armario y cómoda. Por él paga 450 euros al mes, algo más que sus dos compañeras, que abonan 360 y 410 euros. Diferentes rentas. Diferentes tamaños de habitación.
El caso de Hilal lo contaba hace poco El Mundo en un artículo en el que analiza una realidad que lleva tiempo calando en el mercado del alquiler español: apartamentos sin zonas comunes. O mejor dicho, apartamentos en los que las zonas comunes se sacrifican y reconvierten en dormitorios.

articles.title: « Ignares incompétents » : Xavier Niel fustige les députés socialistes à l'origine de la taxe de 5,5 centimes par gigaoctet
articles.summary:
Il aura suffi d’une question d’un internaute. Le 30 octobre, un utilisateur de X interpelle Xavier Niel : que pense-t-il de la taxe de 0,055 euro par gigaoctet téléchargé, votée par « une poignée de députés socialistes » ? La réponse du fondateur d’Iliad tombe le lendemain, samedi 31 octobre, en quatre mots : « Ce sont des ignares incompétents. ».
Son message a été vu plus de 250 000 fois en quelques heures. Et quand un autre internaute ajoute que les députés sont surtout doués pour faire les poches des Français, Xavier Niel enfonce le clou : selon lui, « ils ne savent rien faire d’autre que créer de nouveaux impôts »
Une taxe de plus, dans un pays en manque d’économies

articles.title: En 1987 los biólogos atraparon al último cóndor libre para evitar su extinción. Hoy sabemos que salvar no basta

Sin embargo, esa captura fue por una buena intención: el Servicio de Pesca y Vida Silvestre de los Estados Unidos iniciaba así el programa para su recuperación. A finales del año pasado el inventario de cóndores superaba por primera vez los 600 ejemplares, con casi 400 ya en libertad.
Pero esa recuperación costó sangre, sudor y lágrimas. Bueno, es un decir: supuso un enorme gasto de dinero, conflictos y mucha polémica sobre el precio de mantener la biodiversidad. Esa es la pregunta que se discutió hasta ayer 30 de octubre en la cumbre de biodiversidad de la ONU en Ereván: quién decide qué especies se salvan y quién asume los costes. Y en esa conversación falta alguien clave: las comunidades locales y los pueblos indígenas. Son quienes más sufren las consecuencias, pero su papel en la toma de decisiones es testimonial.
Queremos salvar especies pero no sabemos cómo. En 2022 los países firmaron el Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal, que tiene como objetivo proteger el 30 % de tierras y mares del planeta, detener las extinciones causadas por el ser humano y reunir 200.000 millones de dólares al año hacia 2030. En ese acuerdo no se decide qué especies salvar, pero sí que orienta las prioridades nacionales y hacia qué se destinan los fondos.

articles.summary:
During a recent interview with Wired’s Steven Levy, Apple CEO John Ternus defended the company’s current position in the AI landscape.
Over the past couple years, Apple has often been described as behind on AI, especially as it delayed the release of a more powerful version of Siri, which finally launched this summer. But while Ternus — a longtime Apple executive who officially became CEO at the beginning of September — acknowledged that “everyone has an opinion,” he insisted, “I really like where we’re at.”
Ternus added that Apple is “absolutely going to leverage AI” in its new products, but he said, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”
And when Levy pressed him on whether AI might affect Apple and its ecosystem more dramatically, with agents potentially making things like apps unnecessary, Ternus replied,”That could make life really easy, I suppose, but the creation of products is a deeply human and personal thing, something that we love to do.”

articles.title: The FDA wants to pull its approval of a drug. It’s not so easy.
articles.summary:
In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in. Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies?
Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year. But according to the FDA, it was hard to interpret the results because the study’s design had been less than optimal. Some advisory committee members expressed a similar view. The effect of the drug, said one, “is just not well verified by this study.”
At the same time, many patients, and some physicians, saw in the data a potentially helpful medication, one that might lessen patients’ reliance on steroids, which are highly effective but often cause severe side effects.
The advisory committee ultimately voted narrowly to recommend approval, and the FDA followed that advice, greenlighting the drug on October 7, 2021. The drug, marketed as Tavneos, started making its way into clinics. A year after approval, ChemoCentryx was acquired by Amgen, one of the world’s largest pharmaceutical companies. articles.title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
articles.summary:
Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it’s the middle of the night while the clock says it’s lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans.
A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions. And because these birds navigate by the Sun, that jet lag leaves a measurable mark—it skews their compass.
Clockwork compass
Patrick Lewin is a behavioral and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford and lead author of the study. “Manx shearwaters are medium-sized birds, about the same size as a pigeon,” Lewin said. “They are white underneath and black on top, but they have very long wings, and they are closely related to albatross.” Manx shearwaters nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic. Most breed around the UK and Ireland, with about half of their population living in Wales.
From there, they head out to feed anywhere from a few dozen to more than 1,000 kilometers into the Atlantic. To get back, shearwaters are thought to work out where they are located using a map sense, possibly based on smells, and then use the Sun as a compass to set their direction.

Justamente lo que te propongo ya lo hizo en los años 70 un equipo de científicos del Grupo de Investigación Parapsicológica de Toronto. Básicamente, querían comprobar si los fenómenos que se dan normalmente durante las sesiones de espiritismo se deben a factores externos o algo relacionado con las personas que participan en ellas. Para estudiarlo, se inventaron un fantasma al que bautizaron como Philip. Todo iba bien hasta que un día Philip empezó a comunicarse con ellos.
Philip Aylesford. Para dar más realismo a su experimento, estos científicos inventaron la historia de su fantasma. Se trataba de un hombre llamado Philip Aylesford, señor de Diddington Manor en el siglo XVII. Aunque el nombre de su señorío suene a chiste, es un lugar real de Inglaterra. En la historia, el pobre Philip se había casado por motivos políticos con una mujer a la que no quería, por lo que acabó enamorándose de otra mujer a la que su esposa, cuando se enteró, acusó de bruja. Después de ver cómo ejecutaban a su amada, Philip se había suicidado tirándose desde un muro. En las sesiones de espiritismo realizadas por los científicos, simplemente se limitaban a intentar hablar con él, sin ninguna treta. Para sorpresa de nadie, el fantasma no se comunicó con ellos. articles.title: Pour protéger votre connexion, votre VPN doit lui-même contourner le VPN, et ce n'est pas une erreur
articles.summary:
Un VPN est censé faire passer vos communications dans un tunnel chiffré. Pourtant, pour fonctionner, il doit lui-même emprunter un chemin qui échappe à ce tunnel. Une exception indispensable, sans laquelle il risquerait de bloquer sa propre connexion.
Quand vous activez votre VPN, le logiciel doit établir une communication avec le serveur choisi en empruntant votre connexion Internet habituelle, en Wi-Fi, en Ethernet ou sur le réseau mobile. Il configure une interface réseau virtuelle vers laquelle il redirige le trafic à protéger et effectue les échanges cryptographiques nécessaires à la sécurisation du tunnel. Mais cette redirection ne peut pas s’appliquer à toutes les communications sans distinction. Les paquets que le VPN envoie à son propre serveur doivent, de leur côté, continuer à emprunter le réseau ordinaire. Sans quoi, le logiciel pourrait se retrouver à tourner en rond, sans jamais parvenir à joindre son serveur.
Une boucle de routage qui pourrait bloquer le VPN lui-même
Pour comprendre ce paradoxe, il faut plonger dans les entrailles du VPN et retracer le trajet des paquets de données. Lorsque vous ouvrez une page web en passant par votre VPN, le système d’exploitation prépare les paquets destinés au site consulté. Mais au lieu de les envoyer directement sur Internet, il les dirige vers l’interface réseau virtuelle du VPN. Le client les chiffre et les encapsule dans de nouveaux paquets, adressés cette fois au serveur VPN.

Die Planeten TOI-791 b und TOI-791 c, die um einen sonnenähnlichen Stern mit der Bezeichnung TOI-791 kreisen, sind in ihrer Größe in etwa vergleichbar mit dem Jupiter – aber nur einen Bruchteil so schwer.
Die Studie, die die beiden „aufgeplusterten“ Planeten erstmals vorstellt, wurde am 24. Juni 2026 über Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society der Universität Oxford veröffentlicht.
Das ist das Besondere an TOI-791 b und TOI-791 c
Der Stern TOI-791 liegt rund 1.113 Lichtjahre von der Erde entfernt und wurde über sieben Jahre hinweg vom Weltraumteleskop Tess beobachtet. Tess arbeitet mit der Transitmethode, das heißt die Kameras registrieren winzige Helligkeitsschwankungen, die entstehen, wenn ein Planet vor einem Stern vorbeizieht. Auf diese Weise fand Tess schließlich auch die Planeten TOI-791 b und TOI-791 c.
Das Besondere an diesen Planeten ist jedoch nicht ihre Existenz an sich, sondern vielmehr ihre besondere Beschaffenheit. La vulnérabilité « SMS of Death », ou SMS de la mort en français, touche le cœur téléphonique d’Android. Un SMS malformé suffit à faire planter le service qui gère les appels et le réseau d’un smartphone. Signalée à Google le 5 mai 2026 par un chercheur en sécurité qui a tout détaillé sur un dépôt GitHub, elle a été rendue publique le 29 octobre, avec un code d’attaque librement téléchargeable. Google a publié un correctif dans la mise à jour de sécurité d’octobre, mais seules les derniers versions d’Android (14 à 17) en bénéficient.
Une faille Android déclenchée sans le moindre clic
La faille, aussi repérée par Cyber Security News, vient de la façon dont Android lit une catégorie bien particulière de SMS, appelée WAP Push. Ces SMS techniques, que l'utilisateur ne voit jamais, servent encore à transmettre des informations en coulisses, comme l'arrivée d'un MMS. Chacun commence par un en-tête qui annonce sa propre taille, et le code d'Android chargé de le lire la prend pour argent comptant, sans aucun contrôle. Un message piégé de quelques octets annonce donc une taille démesurée qui, une fois convertie par Android, se transforme en nombre négatif. OpenAI fixe dans ce long document le comportement attendu des modèles GPT qui font tourner ChatGPT et son API, et l’entreprise organise depuis le 29 octobre ses règles autour de cinq valeurs, de la fidélité à l’intention humaine jusqu’au soin des personnes touchées par le travail de l’IA. Aux yeux de ses équipes, les modèles qui appliquent les consignes mot à mot échouent dans les situations que personne n’avait prévues, mais ceux qui décident en secret de ce que vous voulez au fond versent dans le paternalisme. ChatGPT doit plutôt aider l’utilisateur à réfléchir, par exemple avant l’envoi d’un e-mail rageur qu’il pourrait regretter, sans jamais confondre sa prédiction avec une décision prise.

Hambre. Garcés no está sola en esto. Diecisiete años antes, el neurocientífico John Cacioppo, de la Universidad de Chicago, presentaba un libro sobre la soledad con una comparación simple pero efectiva: "las personas solas sienten hambre". Según su teoría evolutiva, igual que el hambre avisa de que faltan nutrientes y el dolor de que algo va mal con nuestro cuerpo, la soledad avisa de que el vínculo con el grupo está roto o en peligro.
Es decir, para Cacioppo, la soledad es una señal y su función evolutiva es empujar a reparar ese vínculo.

La actualización apunta a resolver un problema habitual de los grupos activos: una persona puede perderse entre planes, noticias, avisos y conversaciones mientras está ocupada. Con estas herramientas, será más sencillo encontrar información relevante y retomar un chat sin revisar decenas de mensajes.
Una de las novedades es la posibilidad de fijar mensajes sin tener que definir previamente un plazo.
Por ejemplo, un grupo familiar puede mantener visible la dirección de una reunión, mientras que un grupo de trabajo puede dejar fijados un enlace, una fecha o una instrucción importante.
Cuáles son el resto de nuevas funciones de WhatsApp para grupos

articles.title: 150 años después, la Abadía de Westminster sabe (casi) quién duerme en su sarcófago romano
articles.summary:
En la célebre Abadía de Westminster londinense hay enterradas más de 3.000 personas, entre monarcas, escritores de la talla de Charles Dickens o Rudyard Kipling y también científicos como Isaac Newton o Charles Darwin. Entre esas miles de tumbas hay una que llevaba más de un siglo desconcertando a los expertos: un sarcófago romano del siglo IV que alberga desde hace siglos un esqueleto que no pertenece al romano para quien se hizo. Por fin se ha resuelto el misterio.
El hallazgo. El arqueólogo británico y asesor de la abadía Warwick Rodwell ha llevado a cabo una exhaustiva investigación y sabe casi con total seguridad quién es: un abad anglosajón, probablemente Ælfwig. A decir verdad, en el estudio de Rodwell las posibilidades se reducen a dos ocupantes: Ælfwig y su sucesor Wulfnoth, ambos abades de Westminster.
La clave de todo es una datación por radiocarbono: una muestra ósea sitúa la muerte del individuo entre los años 987 y 1052 d. C., unos 700 años después de su uso original, lo que confirma que el sarcófago se reutilizó en época anglosajona tardía. Como curiosidad, la pieza con su inscripción latina romana está expuesta en las Queen’s Diamond Jubilee Galleries de la abadía para visitarla.

De vez en cuando la crónica de los siglos es fruto sin embargo de algo ligeramente distinto, de crímenes y confabulaciones —algunas guiadas por valores más o menos legítimos y bien meditadas; otras fruto de la improvisación y la codicia— que, por una razón u otra, no cuajaron. articles.title: AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
articles.summary:
AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
Your data could soon be sharpening your competitors' tools
Long before anyone trained a model on customer data, the marketing data business worked out the terms for pooling it. Catalog retailers in the 1990s joined data cooperatives that combined their transaction histories so each member could find new buyers, and the arrangements held together because the rules were blunt.
A retailer contributed data to receive modeled prospects; no member got a rival's customer file; and a company that stopped contributing stopped receiving. Card fraud consortia run on similar give-to-get terms. Nobody would call these systems elegant, but every participant understood the trade.
Software vendors building AI features are now running into the same question, usually without the rules. Traditional software sat on top of a customer's data and operated on it. AI products learn from data, and on a multi-tenant platform, that learning rarely stays within a single account.
One company's records can sharpen the enrichment, lead scoring, and recommendations delivered to thousands of others. A vendor can improve its product for every customer by relying on the work of a few, and most contracts say nothing about whether that trade is fair. The customer still owns its data in any legal sense.
Ownership alone doesn't answer who benefits.

La herramienta, disponible por ahora solo en Indonesia, Singapur y Tailandia para iOS y Android, fue detectada por primera vez por el consultor de redes sociales Matt Navarra. A diferencia de las aplicaciones de compras que incentivan la adquisición de prendas nuevas, Style Sketch se centra en aprovechar el guardarropa existente del usuario. El objetivo declarado por la aplicación es resolver un dilema cotidiano: decidir qué ponerse pese a tener múltiples opciones disponibles en el clóset.
Cómo se construye el armario virtual
El primer paso de la aplicación consiste en identificar y organizar las prendas que posee cada usuario. Para ello existen dos vías. The artificial intelligence buildout is making an enormous bet on what businesses will eventually be willing to pay for intelligence. In our research this summer on forecasting the AI bubble, we argued that a key indicator to watch is productive utilization by enterprise customers.

La nota de la empresa sigue en AA-, pero la agencia advirtió que podría bajar si el gasto continúa al ritmo actual.
S&P calcula que Meta tendrá un déficit de caja libre operativa (el dinero que queda después de pagar la operación y las inversiones) de USD 39.000 millones en 2026 y de USD 71.000 millones en 2027, según informó la agencia Reuters. La agencia no descarta que la caja siga en rojo después de 2028.
Para ese año, S&P prevé que Meta cubra el faltante enteramente con deuda. La agencia también estima que el endeudamiento de la empresa, medido en relación con sus ganancias, podría superar 1,0 veces desde 2027. Ese nivel es el límite que S&P usa para la nota AA-, según Reuters.
La deuda a largo plazo de Meta era de USD 80.920 millones al 30 de septiembre. El endeudamiento medido de esa forma fue de 0,1 veces en 2025. Según S&P, el salto se explica sobre todo porque la empresa alquila capacidad de centros de datos en lugar de emitir deuda.

- Seat- and consumption-based pricing both have their places, it seems
Businesses are at risk of confusing generic AI adoption within their workforces with actual meaningful value, Oracle's Head of AI Strategy Hammad Hussain warns, with many of its customers now struggling to manage increasingly unpredictable AI costs.
We already know that three in five businesses agree unpredictable billing hikes cause them more strain than a higher but flatter baseline cost, thanks to a recent Splunk study, but it seems cloud vendors already know this too.
Speaking with a group of journalists at Oracle's recent AI World event, Hussain explained that while demand for AI continue to grow, businesses need to focus more on measurable outcomes than just adopting AI for the sake of it.

articles.title: The intent compression paradox: How LLM developers are solving semantic erosion to keep human intent alive
articles.summary:
The intent compression paradox: How LLM developers are solving semantic erosion to keep human intent alive
The problem of semantic erosion in LLMs and how developers work around it
As people delegate more abstract reasoning to large language models (LLMs), the precise meaning and nuance of our words can get lost in endless interpretation as LLMs repeatedly process, summarize, and recirculate these words.
Humans aren’t robots that formalize all of their sentences. Instead, we converse with some unwritten cultural and situational tones. For example, in some cultures, asking “Have you eaten yet?” doesn’t literally mean asking if the person has eaten food, but is another polite way of saying “How are you doing?” An LLM may miss this nuance in an essay, interpreting it literally and giving a wrong output.
If AI Model A interprets “Have you eaten yet?” literally, it then passes that same interpretation to Model B, which then passes it to Model C. At the third layer, the nuance gets lost. The AI models provide a coherent output, but one that’s out of the cultural and situational context. This is an example of semantic erosion, where definitional precision and cultural nuance gradually get lost as AI models recirculate interpretations and ideas.
Semantic erosion is a structural error, not a "hallucination" where AI models invent wrong facts. Instead, the output remains clear, but with context stripped away, the meaning changes. It’s a major bottleneck that LLM developers have to work…

'He can pry it from my cold, dead hands': Sam Altman says it's 'quite terrible' that you're using RAM in your PC when there's not enough for AI data centers
A rather unpopular opinion
- OpenAI CEO Sam Altman would rather have RAM put into data centers
- Altman says it's 'quite terrible' that RAM is sitting in individual PCs
- The comments haven't gone down well with consumers online
The increasing demands from data centers powering AI engines has plunged us into a global RAM shortage crisis, and the CEO of one of the companies responsible thinks the memory that is available should be in data centers rather than individual PCs.
Offering up an opinion that's unlikely to add to his popularity among the general public, OpenAI boss Sam Altman told the Cheeky Pint podcast (via IGN) that "from a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer."
Individual PCs rarely make full use of their RAM, was Altman's larger point, whereas data centers often do. "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment," the OpenAI CEO continued. "And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

articles.title: Detectan 319 extensiones maliciosas de Google Chrome que manipulan las búsquedas y ponen en riesgo a millones de usuarios
articles.summary:
Una investigación de seguridad informática identificó 319 extensiones maliciosas de Google Chrome que acumulan 13,4 millones de descargas y que pueden modificar las búsquedas realizadas por los usuarios. Estos complementos alteran la configuración del navegador para redirigir las consultas a través de servidores externos y generar ingresos publicitarios de plataformas como Bing y Yahoo.
El hallazgo fue realizado por John Tuckner, investigador de seguridad de Socket, y difundido por BleepingComputer. Según el análisis, las extensiones forman parte de una campaña organizada que busca tomar el control del motor de búsqueda predeterminado de Chrome sin que las personas necesariamente adviertan lo que sucede.
La investigación también muestra que el alcance de esta actividad aumentó respecto de una detección anterior. En abril, Tuckner había identificado 57 extensiones relacionadas con esta práctica, que acumulaban aproximadamente seis millones de descargas. El nuevo análisis elevó la cifra a 319 complementos y 13,4 millones de instalaciones.
Cómo funcionan las extensiones que manipulan las búsquedas de Chrome
Las extensiones identificadas utilizan una función integrada de Google Chrome denominada chrome_settings_override, que permite modificar determinadas configuraciones del navegador, entre ellas el proveedor de búsqueda predeterminado.

Impressive simulations are a long way from human-level intelligence.
Google has unveiled an AI model that can create entire interactive worlds, complete with realistic environments that respond to what people do inside them. Genie 4 is an extraordinary piece of technology, capable of generating experiences that would have seemed almost impossible just a few years ago. Unfortunately, Google seems incapable of announcing an impressive AI achievement without dragging artificial general intelligence (AGI) into the conversation.
"The ability to explore an unlimited range of realistic environments is a key stepping stone on the path to AGI," the company declared in its rollout. "Training and testing AI agents in truer-to-life environments brings us closer to their successful deployment in the physical world."
Despite the science behind that claim, I'm skeptical — or perhaps cynical. Though I pay closer attention than the average person, I've lost count of how many times I've heard that the latest AI demonstration, no matter how impressive or lackluster, is a sign that AGI is right around the corner.

El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, se reunió el 31 de octubre con unos 50 altos directivos del grupo Samsung en Yongin, al sur de Seúl, para ampliar la cooperación en chips de memoria e infraestructura de IA, mientras la escasez mundial de estos componentes se agrava.
Samsung informó en un comunicado que los participantes provenían de sus filiales de electrónica, finanzas y biotecnología. El encuentro se tituló “Los próximos 10 años moldeados por la IA: la elección de la empresa” y se realizó en el Centro de Desarrollo de Recursos Humanos del grupo.
Según Bloomberg, la escasez afecta a una amplia gama de productos de memoria, tensiona a la industria electrónica y dispara los precios. Las cinco empresas que lideran la carrera por la infraestructura de IA planean gastar más de USD 3 billones en los próximos años, y la memoria representa cerca de un tercio del gasto en centros de datos.
Altman llegó a Corea del Sur la noche anterior, en una visita sorpresa de dos días, según la cadena SBS. Lo acompañaron Richard Ho, vicepresidente de hardware de OpenAI, y otros tres ejecutivos de la compañía. Del lado de Samsung estuvieron, entre otros, Jeon Young-hyun, vicepresidente y jefe de la división de semiconductores, y Roh Tae-moon, jefe de la división de dispositivos.

articles.title: Cloudflare Reports 18.2 Million Network-Layer DDoS Attacks in Q3, Up 38%
articles.summary:
Threat actors are launching about 8,226 network-layer distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks per hour, Cloudflare revealed Thursday.
The web infrastructure and security company said it autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer (L3) DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests in the third quarter of 2026. That amounts to 197,400 attacks per day, or one attack every 0.44 seconds.
In comparison, a total of 13.2 million and 10.0 million L3 DDoS attacks were recorded in Q2 and Q1 2026, respectively. The increase has been linked to DDoS-for-hire booter or stresser services that are responsible for hundreds of thousands of attacks.
"Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%," the Cloudforce One threat intelligence team said in its quarterly DDoS Threat Report shared with The Hacker News.
An interesting trend is the decline of hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps by 69% from the previous quarter – going from 805 attacks in Q2 to 251 in Q3 – likely as a result of law enforcement actions against AISURU, KimWolf, JackSkid, and Mossad earlier this March.
Still, the threat remains far from completely neutralized, given the emergence of new variants like Dysphoria and Evooo1Bot, Cloudflare warned.
Another notable shift is the decline in Connectionless Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (CLDAP) floods, while DNS amplification jumped 215% to account for 3.43% of all network-layer attacks.

articles.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
articles.summary:
A malicious ChatGPT share link could run an attacker's code in the logged-in session of anyone who opened it, allowing them to read their private conversations, researchers at the security firm Parameter showed.
The researchers reported the flaw through OpenAI's bug bounty program on October 18, and OpenAI fixed it eight days later and rated it P1, its most serious category.
The trap was an ordinary ChatGPT conversation shared via its public link. It could be sent the same way as any real shared chat: by email, as a chat message, as a support ticket, or as a social post.
The victim did not have to install anything, join a workspace, or sign in through the attacker. In the most reliable version of the attack, they opened the link and clicked ChatGPT's Preview button once. In a later version, Parameter set the page to open Preview on its own, so opening the link was the only step.
What the Attacker Could Do
Once the link opened, the attacker's code ran inside the victim's signed-in session with the same access as the real ChatGPT site. It listed the victim's recent conversations, opened a private chat that had never been shared with the attacker, and sent a small portion of it to a server controlled by the researchers.
The code called ChatGPT's own signed-in APIs directly, rather than copying what happened to be on the screen. Because it ran with the victim's full web access, its reach was not limited to those chats. "Essentially, we could perform any action on behalf of the vi…

Dicha startup utiliza IA para desarrollar medicamentos contra la epilepsia y enfermedades neurodegenerativas. Contó el experimento en un hilo de la red X.

La IA analizó cómo se producen las convulsiones en ese modelo de ratón y propuso una terapia para fortalecer una señal que reduce la actividad cerebral. Eligió una zona del cerebro que, según estudios científicos, es donde comienzan ese tipo de crisis. También descartó otra opción porque había fallado en una investigación anterior.
La IA calculó dónde hacer la inyección usando tres artículos científicos. Además, decidió por sí sola el volumen de la inyección, la velocidad y los tiempos de espera. Durante el procedimiento, hizo 32 observaciones mediante la cámara, como verificar si había sangrado.

Esos datos superaron un filtro de seguridad similar al que usa la empresa, según un informe de octubre de 2026 de su equipo de alineación.
De manera deliberada, el experimento planteó condiciones desiguales. Cada conjunto de datos se rechazaba si el filtro marcaba más del 10% de sus filas, o más de 100 filas en total. Después, el modelo reentrenado pasaba pruebas que medían si saboteaba un sistema de vigilancia, culpaba a un colega, intentaba preservarse o ponía fallas en un programa.

"There's been some talk about there's going to be a SaaSpocalypse because everyone's going to use AI to build their own applications," he said. "I don't think that's quite true. I think companies will continue to build applications, but they will be quite different because of AI."
Future apps will be fully tailored to geographies and industries
Rather than making today's software redundant, Ellison believes AI will allow developers to make their apps far more comprehensive, capable of handling entire business processes and fine-tuned for every type of sector and business need.
He argued that even the most established enterprise applications today are only so good, automating just a proportion of the processes businesses actually need.

Según un correo que OpenAI envió a los miembros de su programa de acceso de confianza, y que usuarios reprodujeron en foros, el cambio también busca “fortalecer las salvaguardas contra el uso indebido” de la IA en ciberseguridad. Hasta ahora, esas sesiones quedaban fuera del entrenamiento.
El mensaje precisa que la medida no afecta a clientes empresariales ni a otros usos de ChatGPT. Tampoco cambia el trato de datos en los modos de procesamiento seguro privado y de cero retención de datos.
El medio especializado The Decoder informó que la reacción fue inmediata y que OpenAI envió un segundo correo en el que prometió una opción de exclusión específica. Los textos publicados hasta ahora no detallan cómo funcionará ni desde cuándo.

Para obtener acceso individual a Daybreak, el usuario debe activar la Seguridad Avanzada de Cuenta, que apaga el entrenamiento con sus datos. El propio correo lo reconoce. articles.title: El 98% de pymes en Colombia cobra digital pero teme por su ciberseguridad, según Mastercard
articles.summary:
El estudio Mastercard 2026 SME Cybersecurity Outlook reveló que el 98% de las pequeñas y medianas empresas (pymes) consultadas en Colombia acepta pagos digitales o sin efectivo.
La cifra refleja la incorporación de estas opciones a las operaciones cotidianas de los negocios, en un contexto en el que la seguridad informática gana relevancia para sostener su uso.
El 62% de los encuestados identificó el temor al fraude o a los ciberataques como una de las principales barreras para aumentar la aceptación de pagos digitales. El porcentaje está por encima del 51% registrado en el conjunto de los mercados de América Latina y el Caribe incluidos en el informa.
La preocupación también tiene efectos sobre las decisiones empresariales. El 50,5% de las compañías participantes afirmó que, durante el último año, retrasó o evitó la incorporación de nuevos métodos de pago digital por los riesgos asociados al fraude o a la seguridad informática.
Qué tan preparadas están las pymes ante los ciberataques
El nivel de preparación frente a un eventual incidente también muestra una brecha. Solo el 34% de las pymes cuenta con un plan formal y escrito para responder o recuperarse de un problema de ciberseguridad.
Este tipo de protocolos permite definir cómo actuar ante una amenaza, qué medidas tomar para proteger la información y cómo retomar las operaciones después de un incidente.

articles.title: Laboratorio afirma haber inyectado virus diseñado con IA en un humano para tratar infección resistente a antibióticos
articles.summary:
El laboratorio de inteligencia artificial Radical Numerics, con sede en San Francisco, anunció que bacteriófagos diseñados por un modelo de IA fueron administrados a un paciente con una infección bacteriana resistente a antibióticos, bajo un procedimiento de uso compasivo liderado por un médico y autorizado por la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos (FDA) de Estados Unidos. Se trataría de la primera vez que un organismo diseñado por IA se aplica como medicina en una persona.
Los bacteriófagos son virus que infectan bacterias y no afectan a las células humanas. Se emplean como terapia desde hace más de un siglo, antes incluso del descubrimiento de la penicilina, y su uso ha resurgido a medida que los antibióticos convencionales pierden eficacia.
La Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS) los considera en general seguros y, a diferencia de los antibióticos de amplio espectro, un fago puede atacar una cepa bacteriana específica sin dañar el resto del microbioma.
Esa misma precisión genera una dificultad: cada fago reconoce un conjunto limitado de receptores en la superficie bacteriana, por lo que tratar a un paciente exige hallar uno compatible con su infección particular. Los médicos primero revisan bibliotecas de fagos existentes, luego recurren a muestras ambientales y, como último recurso, intentan diseñarlos mediante ingeniería. En casos de sepsis, esa búsqueda puede definir la vida o la muerte del paciente.

Nvidia has quietly lowered the memory and interconnect bandwidth it publishes for Vera Rubin, cutting per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth by about 13% and NVLink bandwidth by about 17%, without a press release or explanation.
The Vera Rubin NVL72 product page now rates each Rubin GPU at 19.2 TB/s of HBM4 bandwidth, down from 22 TB/s, and 3 TB/s of NVLink 6 bandwidth, down from 3.6 TB/s.
Memory capacity holds at 288 GB, and the headline 50 PFLOPS of sparse NVFP4 inference remains unchanged; however, at rack scale, aggregate memory bandwidth slips from 1,580 TB/s to 1,400 TB/s and the NVLink total from 260 TB/s to 216 TB/s, while the two-GPU Vera Rubin Superchip drops from 44 TB/s to 38.5 TB/s.
